::: {.callout-note}
## How this project works
Every search result this report uses is stored in the folder `data/`. The
**first** render sends the searches to OpenAlex, Crossref, EconBiz and EconStor
and saves each answer there. This will already been done once you look at this 
file. **Every later render reads the saved answers** and
sends no request at all -- and that includes *you* first run. 
That makes the report reproducible: you get exactly the
numbers in this report, even though the databases keep changing — and you need
no API key to reproduce it.

To run the searches again with today's data, render with
`quarto render report.qmd -P refresh:true`. This needs your own OpenAlex API
key (see the setup below) and overwrites the saved answers.
:::

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
here::i_am("report.qmd")

# Searches with Umlauten (Arbeitszeitverkürzung) need a UTF-8 session: in the
# "C" locale, which R gets when started from some terminals, the umlaut is
# sent as the text "<c3><bc>" and silently matches nothing. RStudio and
# Windows use UTF-8 by default.
if (!l10n_info()$`UTF-8`) invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))

library(here)
library(openalexR)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(httr2)
library(xml2)

# OpenAlex needs a free API key for searches: store it in your user-level
# .Renviron as OPENALEX_KEY=... (usethis::edit_r_environ() opens the file).
# It is only used when a saved answer is missing or refresh = true.
options(openalexR.apikey = Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_KEY"))

dir.create(here("data"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(here("output"), showWarnings = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
```

The helper `cached()` is what makes the report reproducible. It returns the
saved answer from `data/` if there is one. Only if there isn't does it run the
search, save the answer, and note the date in `data/retrieval_log.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: cached
cached <- function(name, expr, needs_key = FALSE) {
  file <- here("data", str_c(name, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(file) && !isTRUE(params$refresh)) {
    return(read_rds(file))
  }
  if (needs_key && !nzchar(Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_KEY"))) {
    stop("data/", name, ".rds is missing and no OPENALEX_KEY is set. ",
         "Add your OpenAlex key to ~/.Renviron and restart R.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  value <- expr # the search runs only here (lazy evaluation)
  write_rds(value, file)

  log_file <- here("data", "retrieval_log.csv")
  log <- if (file.exists(log_file)) {
    read_csv(log_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  } else {
    tibble(object = character(), retrieved = character(), rows = character())
  }
  log |>
    filter(object != name) |>
    bind_rows(tibble(object = name,
                     retrieved = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"),
                     rows = as.character(NROW(value)))) |>
    write_csv(log_file)
  value
}

clean_doi <- function(x) str_to_lower(str_remove(x, "^https://doi.org/"))
short_id  <- function(x) str_remove(x, ".*/")
```

```{r}
#| label: retrieval-dates
log_file <- here("data", "retrieval_log.csv")
if (file.exists(log_file)) read_csv(log_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
```

The table shows when each saved answer was retrieved. These are the dates to
report for the searches.

# Step 3: the search in OpenAlex

The string is the one from the tutorial, built from its concept table. It is
written exactly as in the web interface. Note that the API uses commas to separate
filters, so the string contains none.

```{r}
#| label: query
query <- '("four-day week" OR "four day week" OR "4-day week"
  OR "four-day workweek" OR "working time reduction" OR "work time reduction"
  OR "reduced working hours" OR "reduction in working hours"
  OR "shorter working week" OR "shorter workweek")
  AND (productivity OR productive OR "well-being" OR wellbeing OR satisfaction
  OR burnout OR stress OR absenteeism OR turnover OR performance)'
query <- str_squish(query) # one line, single spaces
```

First only the number of hits — cheap, and enough to compare string versions:

```{r}
#| label: count
n_hits <- cached("openalex_count", needs_key = TRUE, oa_fetch(
  entity = "works",
  title_and_abstract.search = query,
  type = c("article", "review"),
  language = "en",
  count_only = TRUE
))
n_hits$count
```

See how OpenAlex reads the string and note the `stemmed` before each term:
stemming is switched on automatically.

```{r}
#| label: oql
n_hits$x_query$oql
```

Then the records themselves:

```{r}
#| label: fetch
works <- cached("openalex_works", needs_key = TRUE, oa_fetch(
  entity = "works",
  title_and_abstract.search = query,
  type = c("article", "review"),
  language = "en"
))
nrow(works)
```

## The test set

Four papers that a good search should find. Two are closed-access articles
from Elsevier journals, for which OpenAlex has no abstract — exactly the
records that a title-and-abstract search can only find through their titles.

```{r}
#| label: test-set
test_set <- tibble(
  paper = c("Lepinteur, Labour Economics",
            "Mullens & Laurijssen, BMC Public Health",
            "Raposo & van Ours, Economics Letters",
            "Nord & Costigan, Journal of Applied Psychology"),
  doi = c("10.1016/j.labeco.2018.05.010",
          "10.1186/s12889-024-19161-x",
          "10.1016/j.econlet.2009.10.001",
          "10.1037/h0035419")
)

# The test-set records themselves: do they have an abstract in OpenAlex?
test_records <- cached("openalex_test_set", needs_key = TRUE,
                       oa_fetch(entity = "works", doi = test_set$doi))
with_abstract <- test_records |>
  filter(!is.na(abstract), abstract != "") |>
  pull(doi) |>
  clean_doi()

test_set <- test_set |>
  mutate(found_by_string = doi %in% clean_doi(works$doi),
         has_abstract    = doi %in% with_abstract)
test_set
```

For every paper the string misses, look at its title: which words would a
title-only match have needed? Add them to the string, or rely on snowballing
(step 6) to find papers like it — and note the decision in the search log.

## The abstract gap

How many of the hits have no abstract — and where are they concentrated?

```{r}
#| label: abstract-gap
works <- works |>
  mutate(no_abstract = is.na(abstract) | abstract == "")

works |>
  summarise(records = n(), without_abstract = sum(no_abstract),
            share = round(mean(no_abstract), 2))

works |>
  group_by(host_organization_name) |>
  summarise(records = n(), share_no_abstract = round(mean(no_abstract), 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(records)) |>
  head(10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-abstract-gap
#| fig-cap: "Share of hits without abstract, by publication year."
works |>
  group_by(publication_year) |>
  summarise(share = mean(no_abstract)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = publication_year, y = share)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = "Share of records without abstract")
```

Because only titles can match for records without an abstract, these records
are under-represented in the hits — the true gap in the literature is larger.
These numbers belong in the limitations paragraph.

## The result set

```{r}
#| label: fig-years
#| fig-cap: "Hits per publication year."
works |>
  count(publication_year) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = publication_year, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = "Records")
```

```{r}
#| label: journals
works |> count(source_display_name, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)
```

If almost everything comes from a handful of journals of one field, the string
may be speaking only one community's language.

## Two strings, two vocabularies

Terminology bias becomes visible when strings built from different
vocabularies are compared. String A uses only the "four-day week" terms. The
full string adds "working time reduction" and related terms.

```{r}
#| label: compare-strings
string_a <- '("four-day week" OR "four day week" OR "4-day week")
  AND (productivity OR productive OR "well-being" OR wellbeing OR satisfaction
  OR burnout OR stress OR absenteeism OR turnover OR performance)'

works_a <- cached("openalex_string_a", needs_key = TRUE, oa_fetch(
  entity = "works",
  title_and_abstract.search = str_squish(string_a),
  type = c("article", "review"),
  language = "en"
))

only_full <- setdiff(works$id, works_a$id)
c(string_a = nrow(works_a), full_string = nrow(works), only_full = length(only_full))

works |>
  filter(id %in% only_full) |>
  select(publication_year, source_display_name, title) |>
  head(15)
```

# Step 5: the screening sheet

One row per record, records without an abstract first. The sheet is written
to `output/` and rebuilt on every render.

```{r}
#| label: screening-sheet
screening <- works |>
  transmute(id, doi, publication_year, title, source_display_name, abstract,
            abstract_source = if_else(no_abstract, "", "OpenAlex"))
```

## Fill in abstracts from Crossref

Some publishers deposit abstracts with Crossref, the DOI registration agency.
Elsevier and Springer Nature do not, so their abstracts still have to be
copied from the publisher page by hand.

```{r}
#| label: crossref
crossref_abstract <- function(doi) {
  res <- tryCatch(
    request(str_c("https://api.crossref.org/works/", doi)) |>
      req_perform() |>
      resp_body_json(),
    error = function(e) NULL # no record or no access: NULL
  )
  ab <- res$message$abstract
  if (is.null(ab)) NA_character_ else str_squish(str_remove_all(ab, "<[^>]+>"))
}

missing_dois <- screening |>
  filter(abstract_source == "", !is.na(doi)) |>
  pull(doi) |>
  clean_doi()

crossref <- cached("crossref_abstracts", tibble(
  doi = missing_dois,
  crossref = map_chr(missing_dois, \(d) {
    Sys.sleep(0.2) # be polite to the API
    crossref_abstract(d)
  })
))

screening <- screening |>
  mutate(doi_clean = clean_doi(doi)) |>
  left_join(crossref, by = c("doi_clean" = "doi")) |>
  mutate(
    abstract_source = if_else(!is.na(crossref), "Crossref", abstract_source),
    abstract = coalesce(crossref, abstract)
  ) |>
  select(-doi_clean, -crossref)

screening |>
  count(abstract_source = if_else(abstract_source == "", "(still missing)",
                                  abstract_source))
```

```{r}
#| label: write-sheet
screening |>
  mutate(decision_ta = "", reason_ta = "", decision_ft = "",
         reason_ft = "", notes = "") |>
  arrange(abstract_source) |> # records without abstract first
  write_excel_csv(here("output", "screening_sheet.csv"))
```

The decisions are made by hand: copy the sheet, screen, and save the decisions
as `data/screening_decisions.csv` (columns `id`, `decision_ta`, `reason_ta`,
`decision_ft`, `reason_ft`). The flow diagram below is drawn from that file.

# Step 6: snowballing

The seeds here are the two most-cited hits — a simple, reproducible rule for
this demonstration. In a real review, choose two or three *included* papers
that fit your question best, ideally one from a closed-access journal.

```{r}
#| label: snowball
seed_works <- works |> slice_max(cited_by_count, n = 2, with_ties = FALSE)
seed_works |> select(publication_year, title, cited_by_count)
seeds <- short_id(seed_works$id)

snow <- cached("openalex_snowball", needs_key = TRUE,
               oa_snowball(identifier = seeds))
candidates <- snow$nodes |> filter(!oa_input)
new <- candidates |> filter(!short_id(id) %in% short_id(works$id))
c(candidates = nrow(candidates), new = nrow(new))
```

The new records are screened with the same criteria and counted separately in
the flow diagram. Does snowballing find test-set papers that the string missed?

```{r}
#| label: snowball-test-set
test_set |>
  mutate(found_by_snowball = doi %in% clean_doi(candidates$doi)) |>
  select(paper, found_by_string, found_by_snowball)
```

# Digression: a second database — EconBiz

EconBiz needs no key. The helper puts the same terms into the title, abstract
and description fields, because abstracts sit in one of the last two,
depending on the source.

```{r}
#| label: econbiz-query
in_fields <- function(terms, fields = c("title", "abstract", "description")) {
  str_c("(", str_c(fields, ":(", terms, ")", collapse = " OR "), ")")
}
work_terms <- '"four-day week" OR "4-day week" OR "four day week"
  OR "working time reduction" OR "work time reduction"
  OR "reduced working hours" OR "shorter working week"'
outcome_terms <- 'productiv* OR well-being OR wellbeing OR satisfaction
  OR burnout OR stress OR absentee* OR turnover OR performance'
eb_query <- str_squish(
  str_c(in_fields(work_terms), " AND ", in_fields(outcome_terms))
)
```

`from` counts from 1; a fixed sort order (`id asc`) makes the pages fit
together.

```{r}
#| label: econbiz-search
econbiz_search <- function(q, page_size = 500) {
  fetch <- function(from) {
    request("https://api.econbiz.de/v1/search") |>
      req_url_query(q = q, size = page_size, from = from, sort = "id asc") |>
      req_perform() |>
      resp_body_json()
  }
  first <- fetch(1)
  hits  <- first$hits$hits
  while (length(hits) < first$hits$total) {
    page <- fetch(length(hits) + 1)$hits$hits
    if (length(page) == 0) break
    hits <- c(hits, page)
  }
  first_or_na <- function(x) if (length(x)) as.character(x[[1]]) else NA_character_
  map(hits, \(x) {
    urls <- unlist(x$identifier_url)
    tibble(
      id     = x$id,
      source = first_or_na(x$source),
      type   = first_or_na(x$type),
      year   = as.integer(str_extract(first_or_na(x$date), "[0-9]{4}")),
      title  = first_or_na(x$title),
      doi    = first_or_na(str_to_lower(str_remove(
                 str_subset(urls, "doi.org/"), ".*doi.org/"))),
      handle = first_or_na(str_extract(urls, "10419/[0-9]+") |> discard(is.na))
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}

eb_raw <- cached("econbiz_en", econbiz_search(eb_query))
nrow(eb_raw)
```

Drop events, then duplicates within EconBiz — first by DOI, then by title and
year:

```{r}
#| label: econbiz-clean
eb <- eb_raw |>
  filter(type != "event") |>
  mutate(title_key = str_to_lower(str_remove_all(title, "[^[:alnum:]]"))) |>
  filter(is.na(doi) | !duplicated(doi)) |>
  distinct(title_key, year, .keep_all = TRUE)
nrow(eb)
eb |> count(source, type, sort = TRUE)
```

Abstracts for records in EconStor, via its OAI-PMH interface:

```{r}
#| label: econstor
econstor_abstract <- function(handle) {
  oai <- request("https://www.econstor.eu/oai/request") |>
    req_url_query(verb = "GetRecord", metadataPrefix = "oai_dc",
                  identifier = str_c("oai:econstor.eu:", handle)) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_xml()
  abstract <- xml_find_first(oai, ".//dc:description", xml_ns(oai))
  if (inherits(abstract, "xml_missing")) NA_character_ else xml_text(abstract)
}

handles <- eb |> filter(!is.na(handle)) |> distinct(handle) |> pull(handle)
econstor <- cached("econstor_abstracts", tibble(
  handle = handles,
  abstract = map_chr(handles, \(h) {
    Sys.sleep(0.5) # be polite
    tryCatch(econstor_abstract(h), error = function(e) NA_character_)
  })
))

eb <- eb |> left_join(econstor, by = "handle")
eb |> summarise(records = n(), with_abstract = sum(!is.na(abstract)))
```

Compared with OpenAlex, by DOI — records without a DOI are counted
separately:

```{r}
#| label: econbiz-compare
oa_dois <- works |> filter(!is.na(doi)) |> pull(doi) |> clean_doi() |> unique()
eb_dois <- eb |> filter(!is.na(doi)) |> pull(doi) |> unique()

c(only_openalex       = length(setdiff(oa_dois, eb_dois)),
  only_econbiz        = length(setdiff(eb_dois, oa_dois)),
  both                = length(intersect(oa_dois, eb_dois)),
  econbiz_without_doi = sum(is.na(eb$doi)))

eb |> filter(!doi %in% oa_dois) |> count(type, source, sort = TRUE)
```

The German-language literature, which the English-only OpenAlex search
excludes:

```{r}
#| label: econbiz-german
de_terms <- 'Arbeitszeitverkürzung OR "Vier-Tage-Woche" OR "4-Tage-Woche"'
eb_de <- cached("econbiz_de", econbiz_search(in_fields(de_terms)))
nrow(eb_de)
eb_de |> select(year, title) |> head(10)
```

# Step 8: the flow diagram

The diagram needs the screening decisions, which are made by hand and saved
as `data/screening_decisions.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: decisions
decisions_file <- here("data", "screening_decisions.csv")
has_decisions <- file.exists(decisions_file)
if (!has_decisions) {
  cat("No screening decisions yet (data/screening_decisions.csv is missing):",
      "the flow diagram is drawn once they exist.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prisma
#| eval: !expr has_decisions
library(PRISMA2020)

screened <- read_csv(decisions_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |>
  filter(id %in% works$id)

template <- read_csv(system.file("extdata", "PRISMA.csv", package = "PRISMA2020"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
set_n <- function(tab, field, value) {
  if (!field %in% tab$data) stop("Unknown box in PRISMA template: ", field)
  tab |> mutate(n = if_else(data == field, as.character(value), n))
}

sought        <- screened |> filter(decision_ta != "exclude") |> nrow()
not_retrieved <- screened |> filter(decision_ft == "not retrievable") |> nrow()
reasons       <- screened |> filter(decision_ft == "exclude") |> count(reason_ft)
included_db   <- screened |> filter(decision_ft == "include") |> nrow()

# Snowballing: the new records are screened by hand as well; their decisions
# go into data/snowball_decisions.csv (same columns)
snowball_found    <- nrow(new)
snowball_included <- 0L
snow_file <- here("data", "snowball_decisions.csv")
if (file.exists(snow_file)) {
  snowball_included <- read_csv(snow_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |>
    filter(decision_ft == "include") |>
    nrow()
}

counts <- list(
  database_results           = nrow(works),
  duplicates                 = 0,
  records_screened           = nrow(screened),
  records_excluded           = screened |> filter(decision_ta == "exclude") |> nrow(),
  dbr_sought_reports         = sought,
  dbr_notretrieved_reports   = not_retrieved,
  dbr_assessed               = sought - not_retrieved,
  dbr_excluded               = str_c(reasons$reason_ft, ", ", reasons$n,
                                     collapse = "; "),
  citations_results          = snowball_found,
  other_sought_reports       = snowball_found,
  other_notretrieved_reports = 0,
  other_assessed             = snowball_found,
  other_excluded             = str_c("Not eligible, ",
                                     snowball_found - snowball_included),
  new_studies                = included_db + snowball_included,
  new_reports                = included_db + snowball_included
)
for (box in names(counts)) {
  template <- set_n(template, box, counts[[box]])
}

flow <- PRISMA_data(as.data.frame(template))
diagram <- PRISMA_flowdiagram(flow, previous = FALSE, other = TRUE, fontsize = 12)
PRISMA_save(diagram, filename = here("output", "prisma.svg"),
            filetype = "SVG", overwrite = TRUE)
PRISMA_save(diagram, filename = here("output", "prisma.png"),
            filetype = "PNG", overwrite = TRUE)
diagram
```
